events.title: AI as Your BA Partner: Plan Faster. Lead Smarter. Deliver Better.
events.description:
AI can bring speed, structure, and fresh ideas, but you bring the experience, judgment, leadership, and credibility that move a project forward. This session puts the project manager firmly in control and shows how AI can strengthen the work without replacing the person behind it.

Attendees will see practical ways to use AI for project plans, roadmaps, budgets, risk matrices, status updates, stakeholder communication, and decision support. The goal is simple: reduce busywork, improve clarity, and help project managers lead with greater confidence and deliver stronger results.

**Speaker Bio**

Angie Weller is a product, business analysis, and delivery leader with more than 15 years of experience turning complex business needs into actionable plans and measurable results. Her background includes Agile leadership, project and product delivery, stakeholder alignment, roadmaps, budgeting, risk management, process improvement, and large-scale technology transformation.

Angie is actively involved in Central Iowa’s business analysis and project management communities and is passionate about helping professionals use AI to work smarter while keeping human judgment, personality, and leadership at the core.

events.title: Answering Students' Most Asked AI Questions
events.description:
Ivy Conversations

**November 11 @ 7:00 pm – 8:30 pm CST**

Answering Students’ Most-Asked Questions About AI

Join us November 11 for an engaging conversation with three Ivy College of Business graduates as they answer student-submitted questions about artificial intelligence, its impact in the workplace, and how AI is shaping the careers students are preparing to enter.

[More Info](https://www.ivybusiness.iastate.edu/event/ivy-conversations-ai/)

Speakers include:

**Matt Bilunas**, former chief financial and strategy officer, Best Buy.

**Pat Dennis**, pre-sales technical advisor, OpenAI.

**Renee Langeness**, director of data and analytics governance, Principal Financial Group.

This student-driven event is hosted by the Ivy College of Business, with additional support from the Bacon Center for AI Ethics in Business and the ISU Lectures Program. Questions were generated from a spring 2026 survey of Ivy students.

The event is open to the public with no charge for admission. A reception will follow in the Oak Room, adjacent to the Memorial Union Great Hall.

About the speakers

**Matt Bilunas** is an independent director of Genesco Inc. and a member of the Ivy College of Business Dean’s Advisory Council. He previously spent 20 years at Best Buy, including seven years as chief financial officer and an expanded role as chief financial and strategy officer. At Best Buy, Matt led enterprise finance, strategy, corporate development and data analytics, along with several operating functions. He helped guide the company through its turnaround, omnichannel transformation, the COVID-19 pandemic, and subsequent changes in consumer demand. Matt holds a bachelor of science in accounting from Iowa State University. His first job out of college was in the assurance practice at KPMG.

**Renee Langeness** serves as the director of data and analytics governance at Principal Financial Group, where she leads the company’s Enterprise Data Governance and Ethical and Responsible AI programs. She oversees data management and AI policies, standards, and compliance, while managing data domain decisions and technical enablement of governance frameworks. Her strategic focus includes enhancing oversight capabilities, maximizing data and AI value, and mitigating associated risks. Renee holds a bachelor of science in management information systems from Iowa State University. Her first job out of college was as an IT application analyst at Principal.

**Pat Dennis** works on AI transformation at OpenAI, the AI research and deployment company headquartered in San Francisco, California. He helps organizations understand and adopt AI through executive education, hands-on workshops, and practical demonstrations. Before OpenAI, he worked in enterprise data and AI at Salesforce. Pat holds a bachelor of science in marketing and political science from Iowa State University.

events.title: Professional Development Day 2027
events.description:
In today’s fast-paced business environment, project success requires far more than rigid frameworks and static plans. Rapid technological advancements, shifting organizational priorities, and evolving market demands mean that Business Analysts, Project Managers, and Product Leaders must excel in environments where the only constant is change.

"Navigating Ambiguity: Delivering in Times of Constant Change" is Central Iowa’s premier joint professional development conference brought to you by the IIBA Central Iowa and PMI Central Iowa chapters.

This full-day event brings together regional practitioners, executives, and industry pioneers to move beyond surface-level buzzwords. You will gain actionable frameworks, real-world case studies, and practical tools to lead through uncertainty, harness emerging technologies, and consistently deliver high-value outcomes for your organization.

Conference Tracks

Our session line-up is structured around three core tracks designed to deliver immediate, cross-functional value for Business Analysts, Project Managers, Agile Coaches, and Technology Leaders:

Strategic Leadership & Adaptability

Navigating ambiguity at the organizational level. Focuses on executive alignment, managing shifting priorities, driving strategic outcomes, and leading teams through change when direction is fluid.

AI & Tech-Driven Delivery in Flux

Harnessing innovation amidst constant technological shift. Explores practical applications of generative AI, predictive analytics, and automated workflows in requirements elicitation, risk forecasting, and project delivery.

Dynamic Execution & Delivering Value

Adapting execution when traditional frameworks fall short. Covers hybrid delivery models (Agile/Waterfall), continuous backlog refinement, rapid prototyping, and de-risking high-ambiguity initiatives.
